summary: Text-display helper: renders the base dual text via DualTextDisplay, then, when field this+0x8 is nonzero, emits a sequence of formatted lines at stepped offsets. Each line is prepared by a per-line buffer helper and rendered with StringFormatAndRender into the first-region display state v1 (flag 1) and second-region display state v2 (flag 0), using this[2] and the string data at this[5]+84 as content. The final line renders with literal 240 instead of a display-state value.

operations.description: Capture display parameters: v1 = dword_5CCBC0, v2 = dword_7CE238, v3 = dword_5CCBB8.
Render the base dual-text display with DualTextDisplay(dword_5CCBC0, dword_7CE238, dword_5CCBB8).
Read this[2] (field this+0x8); when zero the formatted-line block is skipped and that value is returned.
Compute line offset v6 = dword_5CCBBC + v3.
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49C140(v10, 64).
Render StringFormatAndRender(v10, v1, v6, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 1) with first-region display state v1.
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49C280(v10, 64).
Render StringFormatAndRender(v10, v2, v6, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 0) with second-region display state v2.
Advance line offset v7 = dword_5CCBBC + v6.
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49BDE0(v10, 64).
Render first-region line StringFormatAndRender(v10, v1, v7, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 1).
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49BE50(v10, 64).
Render second-region line StringFormatAndRender(v10, v2, v7, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 0).
Advance line offset v8 = dword_5CCBBC + v7.
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49BF80(v10, 64).
Render first-region line StringFormatAndRender(v10, v1, v8, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 1).
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49BFF0(v10, 64).
Render second-region line StringFormatAndRender(v10, v2, v8, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 0).
Advance line offset v9 = dword_5CCBBC + v8.
Prepare the text buffer with sub_49C0B0(v10, 64).
Final render StringFormatAndRender(v10, 240, v9, this[2], *(this[5]+84), 1); the literal 240 replaces the display-state value.
Return the final render result, or this[2] when the formatted-line block was skipped.
